observability.signal: Canonical applications.json plus generated AppCode surface
observability.expected_result: Exactly ten canonical identities remain versioned and reproducible: shell, anima, viso, nexo, fogo, origo, pulso, numera, aura and pass; hub/default remain non-canonical aliases or configuration values only.

observability.signal: vento-shell launcher, login metadata and template AppSwitcher consumers
observability.expected_result: All three consumers project the canonical identity set and governed lifecycle semantics without local competing identity universes.

observability.signal: NEXO, FOGO, ORIGO, PULSO and VISO runtime application-identity consumers
observability.expected_result: Each runtime repo consumes canonical AppCode semantics consistently across vento-shell.tsx, vento-chrome.tsx and app-switcher.tsx; hub/default are not treated as AppCode members and pass is not silently omitted.
The seven VERIFIED canonical foundation files remain byte-stable while only discovered consumers and GAP-PKG-045 evidence targets change.

observability.signal: Product, Supabase and production mutation delta outside discovered identity consumers
observability.expected_result: Zero unrelated product, database, Supabase or production mutations; changes remain constrained to the exact physical targets in this dossier.

acceptance_criteria: physical_discovery is COMPLETE, traceable, has zero unresolved findings and covers physical_identity.targets exactly 1:1.
applications.json remains the sole versioned source for the ten canonical application identities and generated AppCode surfaces remain reproducible from it.
hub and default are not treated as canonical AppCode identities in launcher, APP_ENTITY or AppSwitcher logic; shell is the canonical Vento OS application identity.

Vento Pass is not silently lost from canonical application identity projections merely because it is a customer/mobile-adjacent product; availability and destination behavior must be explicit and fail closed where no web destination is approved.

AURA catalog membership remains distinct from product availability; runtime presentation must not infer product readiness solely from lifecycle_status=active when canonical product-existence governance says the application is not currently available.
The central launcher, login metadata and AppShell template no longer maintain competing application identity lists that contradict the canonical contract.
NEXO, FOGO, ORIGO, PULSO and VISO runtime AppSwitcher/APP_ENTITY consumers no longer maintain competing application identity universes or hub/default AppCode aliases.
The existing SHELL-CON-002::GLOBAL foundation remains byte-stable and is adopted without modification.
TREQ-SHELL-003, TREQ-SHELL-028 and TREQ-SHELL-034 retain explicit deterministic package-specific evidence in tests/packages/GAP-PKG-045.
All vento-shell package validations plus npm test and typecheck in each of the five runtime consumer repositories pass before CI020 can be VERIFIED.
No Supabase mutation or database migration is created or changed by GAP-PKG-045.
Production remains unauthorized; only governed staging-safe implementation and validation are permitted.
rollback_steps: If implementation fails before publication, revert only GAP-PKG-045 consumer changes and package-specific evidence artifacts in their authorized repositories; do not modify or revert the VERIFIED SHELL-CON-002::GLOBAL foundation.
If any runtime consumer cannot be reconciled without a new undiscovered repository/path/surface, stop CI020 and re-mature again before making that new delta.
If a consumer regression appears, restore that repository consumer file to its pre-CI020 state and keep the package unverified until canonical identity semantics and repository tests pass.
No database rollback is required because Supabase/database mutation is outside this package scope.
After rollback, rerun canonical catalog generation/validation, all GAP-PKG-045 package tests and the affected consumer repository test/typecheck commands.
